fields.meta_title: Booking Form Builder With Open Slots and Deposits | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a booking form that shows only open times and takes a deposit before it confirms. Every booking lands in a database you own.
fields.h1: Build a Booking Form That Only Offers Open Times
fields.hero_description: Describe what people book and who may book it. Emergent builds the booking form and the schedule behind it, hiding taken slots and collecting deposits before a date is confirmed.
fields.features_heading: What a Booking Form Has to Get Right
fields.features_subheading: Anyone can ask for a date and a time. The real work is making sure the time on offer is still free.
fields.feature_1:
Slots drawn from your own schedule

Set opening hours and blackout dates once, plus a buffer between bookings. The slot picker reads that schedule and the bookings table, then offers only the times still free.
fields.feature_2:
One slot, one booking

Hold a time the moment someone submits. When two people pick the same 3:00 PM slot, the second one sees the next open time instead, and every answer they typed stays filled in.
fields.feature_3:
Questions that change with the service

Show different fields for each thing being booked. A furnace repair asks for the model number, a portrait session asks how many people are coming and a room asks nothing extra.
fields.feature_4:
Deposits through your Stripe account

Connect Stripe and take a deposit or the full price before a booking confirms. An unpaid hold expires after the window you choose, and each payment is saved on its booking row.
fields.feature_5:
Confirmations and reschedule links

Send a confirmation email when a booking lands and a reminder before it starts. Each message carries a link to move or cancel, and any time given up goes back into the picker.
fields.feature_6:
Code that leaves with you

Publish the booking form on your own domain or embed it in the site customers already use. Export the full code to GitHub when a developer wants it inside a larger system.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Businesses, Four Kinds of Booking
fields.tab_content_1:
Without the safety course, no laser time

Foundry Makerspace rents its laser cutter in 2-hour blocks. Members type in a member number first, and Emergent checks it against the shop's training records. Those with the laser safety course on file pick from the open blocks. Anyone without it sees the next class date and a sign-up link.
fields.tab_content_2:
Up to three jobs in every arrival window

Brightline Appliance Repair has three vans and caps each 4-hour arrival window at three jobs. Customers enter a ZIP code and the appliance, then choose a window with room left. Full windows drop off the form. Addresses outside the 14 ZIP codes Brightline covers get the office phone number instead of a slot.
fields.tab_content_3:
Pay $150 or the date reopens in 24 hours

Wren Hollow Photography will not hold a Saturday on a promise. Clients pick a date and a session type, then pay a $150 deposit on a Stripe checkout page. An unpaid date is released after 24 hours. For a $600 family session, the remaining $450 is requested by email seven days before the shoot.
fields.tab_content_4:
The 11th room hour shows its $25 price first

Every desk at Harbor Street Commons comes with 10 meeting-room hours a month. Each room request shows the member how many of those hours are left. Time past the allowance is priced at $25 an hour before the member confirms, and it goes on their account for the month.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Booking Form
fields.howto_description: Work out what is scarce and who may claim it. The fields are the easy part.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Decide who is allowed to book
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down each thing that can be booked, whether it is a machine or a person's time. Next to each one, note how long a booking lasts and how many can run at once. Those two numbers decide every time the form can offer.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Some bookings are open to anyone. Others need a trained member or an address inside your service area. Pick the detail that proves eligibility, such as a member number or a ZIP code. The form asks for it before showing any times.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Choose whether a booking needs money up front. A deposit makes sense for work that blocks out a whole day, and a free booking suits a short call. Write down how long an unpaid hold lasts and what happens to the date afterward.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Write both emails in your own words. Tell people what to bring, where to park and how to reschedule. Pick how far ahead the reminder goes out, such as the afternoon before, and who gets a copy when a booking is canceled.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste your notes into Emergent in plain English. It builds the form, the availability rules and a bookings table you own. If your staff live in Google Calendar, ask Emergent to add each booking there through the Google Calendar API.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Open the form on a phone
fields.howto_step_6_des: Book a slot on a phone the way a customer would. Then try to take that same slot from a second browser, skip the deposit and enter an address outside your area. Each attempt should fail exactly the way your notes say it should.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Publish and read the first week
fields.howto_step_7_des: Put the form live on your domain, or embed it on the page where customers already look for you. Read every booking in the table for the first week. Times that fill within hours and times nobody takes show where to add availability and where to cut it.

plan.angle: The top 10 is template galleries (Jotform, Typeform, Canva, Fillout, forms.app, Dribbble) that hand over fields, plus scheduling-tool blogs (YouCanBookMe, OnceHub) that sell a fixed calendar. A booking form is a request against something scarce: a machine, a van, a photographer's Saturday, a room. This page shows Emergent building the form together with the availability behind it, so a slot disappears once it is taken, eligibility is checked before times appear and a deposit decides whether a hold becomes a booking. It answers the Google PAA questions neutrally and points to the reservation and template searches with practical answers.
